newsitem.title: USA: Trade group seen challenging SBC long-distance bid.
newsitem.headline: Trade group seen challenging SBC long-distance bid.

text.p: An industry trade group is expected soon to ask federal regulators to dismiss SBC Communications Inc's application to offer long-distance service from Oklahoma, sources said Friday.

The Association for Local Telecommunications Services, or ALTS, is expected to make a filing with the Federal Communications Commission next week, said the sources, who requested anonymity. An ALTS official declined to comment.
The trade group, which represents competitive providers of local phone service, is expected to argue that SBC does not face competition in the residential phone business in Oklahoma.
Under the 1996 communications law, SBC and the other regional Bells must meet a 14-point checklist showing they had opened their local monopolies before gaining FCC approval.

SBC's bid to be the first Baby Bell to enter the $80 billion long-distance business was thrown into doubt earlier this week after an Oklahoma regulator said the carrier failed to meet the entry terms.
SBC has said it remains confident that it will prevail.
